tag: Episode 52 · A Promise by the Cherry-Blossom River
title: A Promise by the Cherry-Blossom River

beats.t: Monday. The moment classes ended, Yeoni took their bicycle to the riverbank. Eastern waterside. Before the blossoms fall. Those were all the clues.
Tuesday, three bridges. Wednesday, five. No white umbrella anywhere. Only cherry blossoms falling faster each day.
Once all the flowers fall, that's it? Are readings that cruel?
[ App notification · Kang Saebyeok: Thursday. Last day before the blossoms fall. Your daily fortune looks good. Reading fee later. ]
Why charge me? Do you know how many kilometers that eastern waterside covers? Pay for my calves first.
Even so, Yeoni pedaled. Today they'd deliberately worn mismatched socks. Yellow on the left, stripes on the right.
A test. If it's really him, he won't let this pass.
Putting on those socks that morning, Yeoni had laughed alone. The world's strangest investigation method.
[ App notification · Moka: Found him? If not, I'll cheer you on with rap. Yo yo, Mr. Park, where you at? ]
That's interference, not encouragement.
Wind blew from the river. A handful of petals fell from a cherry tree on the embankment. Yeoni started counting them, then stopped. Counting made them more anxious.
What if it really ends when the flowers fall? With him still not knowing me?
Yeoni gripped the handlebars. The center of their palm felt slightly warm. Where the Metal fragment had stayed.
Four in the afternoon. The seventh bridge. Yeoni collapsed onto a riverside bench. Their calves felt ready to burst. The bicycle fell beside them.
One star. Universe Customer Support, one star. No, half a star.
Yeoni opened their notebook. Possibly white hair. Obsessed with socks. Sensitive about ratings. White umbrella. Cat allergy. Toward the river.
I've written so much. Still can't picture his face.
As they closed the notebook, a petal settled between the pages. Yeoni left it there instead of brushing it away.
Then a sneeze came from the far end of the bench. Yeoni turned.
A white umbrella leaned against the bench. Beside it sat a man with a book open on his knees. A stray cat crouched at his feet.
Ah, sorry. I'm allergic to cats.
Then why not shoo it away?
It sat here first. This is its spot.
One strand of the man's hair was white, as though naturally so rather than dyed. His eyes were reserved, his voice low.
Yeoni held their breath. Their heart pounded up to their ears. No certainty. Plenty of people had white hair.
Your bicycle fell over.
Oh. Yes. I know. Deliberately.
Never met someone who knocks it over deliberately.
The man looked back at his book, then stopped. His gaze caught at Yeoni's ankles, between the yellow sock and the striped one.
Excuse me. Your socks don't match.
Yeoni couldn't answer. They bit their lip. Their eyes burned. Looking alarmed, the man closed his book.
Oh, sorry. What a strange thing to say. I don't know why I said it. To someone I've just met.
It's okay. I used to hear it every day.
Every day? From whom?
Someone who scolded a lot. I thought he was an ordinary cat at first. He wasn't. Later, he became human.
The man tilted his head. An unbelievable story, yet he didn't laugh it off. At that expression, Yeoni laughed through tears.
Where is he now?
He went home. Very far away. Barely said goodbye.
He's made you wait a long time.
Right? Completely irresponsible. His last words were about socks.
That was a bit much. Strangely, I feel guilty.
Without noticing, he rubbed his temple like someone developing a headache. Yeoni didn't miss the gesture.
Somehow, they began walking together. He righted the bicycle, Yeoni thanked him, and they were going the same way. That was all.
The cherry-tree path stretched along the river. Petals blew onto their shoulders. The last petals.
May I tell you something strange? I keep having the same dream lately.
What dream?
Walking this path with someone carrying a yellow umbrella. Sometimes there's a pig. With pink flowers.
A pig?
Thought it meant lottery luck, so I bought tickets three times. All lost.
It's not a lottery dream. Really.
Then what is it? Do you interpret dreams?
Apparently pigs mean you'll meet someone who helps you. I just made that up.
The man looked as though he didn't know why they were laughing. Yeoni couldn't stop. A petal caught in his white strand of hair.
Excuse me. What's your name?
Park Byeongha. Yours?
Park Byeongha. Yeoni rolled the name silently in their mind. The name first read at the Lovers card. The name that would make him disappear.
That rule belonged to the other world. Yeoni had written on Card Twenty-Three themselves: The door opens from inside too.
Still. That name was given by someone else.
Yeoni shook their head. There was another name to call. One they'd given him. One tied to a one-star rating.
I'm Yeoni. And may I ask a favor?
What is it?
I'm going to say a strange name now. You don't have to answer. Just listen.
Neo.
The wind stopped. Falling petals seemed to pause briefly in midair. Park Byeongha stopped walking.
Ah.
He pressed his forehead as though in pain and closed his eyes. Something raced beneath his eyelids.
A rainy bus stop. An inside-out umbrella. A cat's place at the foot of a bed. The sun of the Island of Expression. A dragon egg in a vault. Drowned bookshelves. White light inside the Void.
And Yeoni, first taking his human hand on the boat above the river. The warmth against his shoulder then.
Yeoni.
Yes. It's me. Mismatched socks.
Decided on the rating? You said you'd tell me when you did.
His manner of speaking had changed. Blunt, a little cheeky, strangely gentle at the end. The voice Yeoni knew.
Five stars. Almost took one off for being late, but I didn't. The review will be long, though.
Generous.
Yeoni gripped his shirt and cried. Byeongha hesitated briefly, then wrapped his arms around their back. This time, no part of him faded.
My hands don't show through now. Holding you like this... is okay, right?
My head. Just my head. You know how to pat it.
And Yeoni. Why are your socks mismatched again?
A test. You passed.
The stray cat following at their feet meowed. Park Byeongha sneezed. Yeoni laughed aloud.
The allergy survived. Couldn't they have fixed that when I returned? I'll have to call customer support myself.
Let's file a complaint. Only one person in the queue. Should connect quickly.
Do you really remember everything? Being Park-whatever and being Neo, both?
Both. Byeongha, going to work and paying rent. Neo, beside you. Even the hand you took on the boat.
Strangely, none of it gets mixed up. Maybe because both are me.
Then what should I call you? Byeongha? Neo?
The name you gave me. Yeongnyangi. Byeongha around other people. If you call me Yeongnyangi at work, explanations get long.
I wasn't planning to visit your office. Now I am.
Byeongha laughed. A slightly awkward smile with one corner rising first. Yeoni felt they would never forget it now.
The sun tilted over the river. Petals drifted slowly on the water. They stood side by side against the riverside railing.
I walked this path in a dream. In an ordinary spring. With you.
What did we do in the dream? Don't tell me we fought.
Nothing. Just walked. That was the best part. We fought after I woke.
Then promise. Every spring, we walk here. Before the blossoms fall. Doing nothing.
Promises are made to be kept. If it rains, you carry the umbrella. The yellow one.
[ App notification · Seo Hanbi: Sea trip, second Saturday in May. One more person is welcome. No one who sheds fur. ]
Haven't shed fur in ages. Still bringing that up?
You still sneeze.
Yeoni replied: Adding one. Human. No fur. Sock inspector.
[ App notification · Kang Saebyeok: You found him. My daily forecast was right, so the fee is due. Also, his birth time, please. ]
Why is he still asking birth times?
He wants to read our compatibility. Yours and mine.
The Eul–Gyeong union is enough for us. We came all this way together.
Still curious, though. What score we'd get.
If it's not a hundred, give that fortune-teller one star.
Smiling, Yeoni pocketed the phone and took Park Byeongha's hand. A human hand was larger than expected, and a little colder.
Your hand's cold. Because you're Gyeong Metal?
Your hand's warm. Because you're Eul Wood.
Hand in hand, they walked along the river. The stray cat followed at a distance. Park Byeongha sneezed again. The last petal drifted downriver.
